message.reasoning:
I am reviewing the current Monopoly game state to determine the best move.

I have $2314 cash and am at ST_CHARLES_PLACE. I own four houses on every color group: brown, pink, and orange. Most of my other properties are mortgaged.

I have two get-out-of-jail cards. The opponent has $110 cash and all properties mortgaged, including Pacific Avenue. Players three and four are bankrupt. The bank has no houses left but still holds twelve hotels.

I have just collected $200 for passing GO. I will not build hotels or unmortgage properties because that returns houses to the bank. The opponent has only $110 cash and no properties. I am now calculating rent values to determine the best action.

Mediterranean Avenue with four houses costs $160. That is enough to bankrupt the opponent, who has only $110 cash. The best move is to end the turn and wait for them to land on my properties.

Unmortgaging the three railroads would cost $330. Their rent would only be $100, which is less than the opponent's $110 cash. That would not bankrupt them. I will not unmortgage any properties.

Utilities are not worth unmortgaging. The maximum rent is only $120, and the opponent's roll is unknown.

The light blue set would cost about $176 to unmortgage and would still allow no house building.

I now see that all three yellows are mortgaged. Unmortgaging them would give me a complete set and allow house building. I will unmortgage the yellows.

Unmortgaging the yellows would cost $286. Even with a yellow monopoly, base rent is only about $44 to $48 per space. That is still below the opponent's $110 cash, so it will not bankrupt them. I have no green monopoly either.

The opponent owns the complete red set but has mortgaged every property. Unmortgaging all three would cost $374, which exceeds their $110 cash. They cannot unmortgage the reds.

Every developed property kills the opponent. Hotels waste cash and return houses to the bank. I am now on CHANCE and worried that a lucky card could give the opponent enough money to survive.

A single chance card would not give the opponent enough money to unmortgage the red set. Two might, but that is unlikely. I will not build hotels or return houses. Trading with the opponent would only help them survive, so that is not an option.

I will not mortgage Marvin or North Carolina. That would waste cash and reduce my rent income. I am now considering selling houses.

Selling houses would lower rent and return them to the bank. That is dangerous because the opponent could survive on a property like Mediterranean Avenue. The correct move is to end the turn.
